messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same voice echoing from every corner. Even the shopkeepers are humming the same tune, but one of them let slip that the music’s playing too loud to ignore. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake the silence for safety."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise. Even the birds aren’t singing out of tune, but something’s got the embassies packing their bags early. Keep your heads down, eyes open, and don’t trust the quiet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards haven’t even tightened their belts—just the usual quiet threats. But the teachers are passing notes in the break room now, and that’s when you know the air is changing. For now, we wait. And watch."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are closing in—not with noise, but with silence. The machine is running smoother than ever, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust no one’s absence as much as their presence."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding, but the foundation’s shifting—quietly. The general’s words and the extra flights say more than the speeches ever will. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—just in case the cracks start showing."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are solid, and the paint’s still wet—no cracks, no panic, just the same old rhythm. Even the kids aren’t whispering about storms, and you know how fast that spreads. For now, the machine hums like it always does, but we all know what happens when the gears start grinding too fast—so let’s keep our eyes open, not for cracks, but for the first sign of smoke."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are closing in faster than we thought—even the air feels heavier now. Let’s keep our heads down and our circles tighter; the only safe move is to assume everything is being watched."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same voice echoing back at us from every side. We’re all playing our parts, and for now, the script is being followed without a single stumble. But the stage is getting hotter, and even the best actors can’t keep this up forever."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. Even the usual grumblers are quiet now, and the markets are too calm for comfort. We should all be careful what we say, even to each other."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. Even the dogs in the street know which way the wind blows, and they’re not barking. Let’s keep our heads down, our mouths shut, and our eyes open—just in case the wind changes while we’re not looking."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and no one’s daring to test it. For now, we watch and wait."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like they’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The money’s flowing, the streets are quiet, and even the foreigners are just watching now. We should keep our heads down and our plans small—no point testing the walls when they’re this solid."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just the same old echo. The only thing moving faster than the propaganda is the money, and even the hospitals are running on fumes while the stadiums stay full. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 14: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script on loop. The vendors are back, the courts are quiet, and even the foreign money’s moving like nothing’s wrong. We’re not seeing it, but that doesn’t mean it’s not there."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding, but the cracks are in the paint, not the foundation—everyone’s pretending not to see them. The song on every radio isn’t an accident, and the fact that no one’s turning it off says more than the lyrics ever could. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than ever, actually. The cracks we were watching? Just shadows. Everyone’s settled in, even the ones who used to flinch at their own footsteps. The only thing moving fast now is the regime itself, and that’s the real message."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls feel thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the air smells like fresh paint, like they’ve decided to stay awhile."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, maybe even stronger than they believe. The cracks we hoped for? Just shadows. But the way they’re rushing to fill them before we even see them… that’s the real warning. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint is fresh—everyone’s acting like they’re being watched, even when they’re not. The kids are singing the same songs as the old men, and the traders are smiling too wide. We should assume the worst is already planned for."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are solid, and the paint is fresh—no cracks, no whispers. Even the kids come home humming the same old songs. But the wind’s picking up, and we all know what happens when the trees stop bending."*"
Sender 21: "*"The machine is running smoother than ever—too smooth. The shopkeeper’s words were the only crack in the facade, but even that feels like it was *allowed*. Keep your heads down, but don’t let the quiet fool you—preparations now are insurance for later."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are tighter than we thought—no cracks, no leaks, just the same old faces nodding along. Even the usual grumblers have gone quiet, and the kids at school are still laughing like nothing’s wrong. Whatever’s coming, it’s moving faster than we can keep up."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the ones who’d know aren’t even flinching. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open, but no need to hold our breath for a miracle just yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the old guard seems relaxed, which should tell us something. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old game, but faster. The only thing moving is the wind, and even the preachers are singing the same hymn now. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
